observations: The completion scope is GOAL-CMVA-01 and its frozen policy; Unity/platform/load-finalization and future roadmap work remain outside this closure.

The reviewed development criterion v3 is per-phase elapsed 6000000000 ns, allocator peak 1342177280 bytes, RSS 1610612736 bytes and native requested 233000000. It is an explicit measured admission criterion, not a new gameplay operation cap, default-profile rewrite or universal latency guarantee.

Expanded 500/1000 employee workloads are actual finite roster/asset workloads with eight deployed actors; normal has sixteen roster employees and one deployed actor. The three repeated four-phase scenarios and actual coverage are the bounded evidence, not arbitrary combat scalability.

Actual resource-only base native maximum 230987820 is close to the 233000000 criterion. This is accepted versioned development scope with raw margin visible, not a promise across unmeasured machines/builds.
Historical U10 PC strict failures, 31-success/5-rejection context and R05 peak-only/environment limits remain unchanged; U11 does not certify all platforms or claim a full-suite rerun.

Plain native zero is uninstrumented, not zero cost. Peak heap, OS RSS, cumulative native requests and end-live allocator values are distinct; retained active generations and process allocator retention are not conflated.

Early evidence is reused only for unaffected predicates. Later current-owner builds/criteria and affected-path oracles supplement changed consumers. Historical failed, timeout, incomplete, context-irrelevant and zero-test records keep their original status.
Normal approval requires the declared bounded supported suite and exact coverage. Diagnostic/raw Core embedding remains available for its trusted purpose and has no normal issuer authority.
This audit executed read-only parsing/hashing/archive inspection only. It did not rerun gameplay, performance, compilation, or workspace restoration.
